estat

Random-effects covariance matrix

Stata 

estat recovariance

R lme4 

as.matrix(lme4::VarCorr(fit)$id)

Differs from Stata Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Estimated covariance conditional on the chosen random-effects structure.

Stata reference · R reference

1 more examples and alternatives

Variance components as standard deviations and correlations

Stata 

estat sd

R lme4 

as.data.frame(lme4::VarCorr(fit))

Differs from Stata Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Includes residual standard deviation and random-effect correlation.

Stata reference · R reference

mecloglog

Complementary-log-log random-intercept model with Laplace approximation

Stata 

mecloglog binary x || id:, intpoints(1)

R lme4 

lme4::glmer(binary ~ x + (1 | id), data = data, family = stats::binomial(link = "cloglog"), nAGQ = 1, control = lme4::glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa"))

Differs from Stata Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Stata's integration settings must be matched; one Laplace point differs from adaptive quadrature.

Stata reference · R reference

Complementary-log-log random-intercept model with adaptive quadrature

Stata 

mecloglog binary x || id:, intpoints(9)

R lme4 

lme4::glmer(binary ~ x + (1 | id), data = data, family = stats::binomial(link = "cloglog"), nAGQ = 9, control = lme4::glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa"))

Differs from Stata Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Stata's integration settings must be matched; one Laplace point differs from adaptive quadrature.

menbreg

Negative-binomial mixed model with quadratic mean variance

Stata 

menbreg nb x || id:, intmethod(laplace)

R glmmTMB 

glmmTMB::glmmTMB(nb ~ x + (1 | id), data = data, family = glmmTMB::nbinom2())

Differs from Stata NB2 with a Gaussian random intercept and Laplace likelihood. Stata intmethod(laplace) explicitly matches the approximation. R dispersion is the inverse of Stata NB2 alpha; compare transformed ancillary parameters.

Stata reference · R reference

menl

Nonlinear exponential growth with random asymptote coefficient

Stata 

menl y = {A}*exp({B}*x), define(A: {a0}+{U[id]})

R nlme 

nlme::nlme(y ~ A * exp(B * x), data = data, fixed = A + B ~ 1, random = A ~ 1 | id, start = c(A = 2, B = .25))

Differs from Stata Gaussian nonlinear mixed model with random subject amplitude A and a common exponential rate B. Both fit by ML. Starting values are numerical aids, not a restriction on parameter estimates.

Stata reference · R reference

mixed

REML random-intercept model

Stata 

mixed y x || id:

R lme4 

lme4::lmer(y ~ x + (1 | id), data = data, REML = FALSE)

Differs from Stata REML=FALSE explicitly matches Stata mixed default ML. lme4 does not print Stata large-sample fixed-effect z tests by default; match covariance structures and request the intended inference separately.

Stata reference · R reference

Independent random intercept and slope

Stata 

mixed y x || id: x, covariance(independent)

R lme4 

lme4::lmer(y ~ x + (x || id), data = data, REML = FALSE)

Differs from Stata REML=FALSE explicitly matches Stata mixed default ML. lme4 does not print Stata large-sample fixed-effect z tests by default; match covariance structures and request the intended inference separately.

Stata reference · R reference

Correlated random intercept and slope

Stata

R lme4 

lme4::lmer(y ~ x + (x | id), data = data, REML = FALSE)

Differs from Stata REML=FALSE explicitly matches Stata mixed default ML. lme4 does not print Stata large-sample fixed-effect z tests by default; match covariance structures and request the intended inference separately.
